concepts.title: Physical Change
concepts.definition: A transformation where a substance alters its physical traits like shape, size, or state without forming any new chemical substance.
concepts.key_idea: Physical changes are typically reversible and do not produce new matter.
question_patterns: identify if cutting paper is a physical change
what are the characteristics of a physical change
is melting of ice a physical or chemical change
classify the following as physical change
what do you understand by physical change

solution_steps.action: Observe the substance before and after the change
solution_steps.explain: Check if the chemical identity remains the same.
If no new substance is created, it is a physical change.
Most physical changes like melting or freezing can be reversed.

compute_steps.action: substitute the given values into the formula

concepts.title: Chemical Change
concepts.definition: A process where one or more materials react to create entirely new substances with different properties.
concepts.key_idea: Chemical changes are usually irreversible and accompanied by energy changes or gas evolution.
question_patterns: define a chemical change with examples
what happens during a chemical reaction
is digestion of food a chemical change
list signs that indicate a chemical change has occurred
how does chemical change work

solution_steps.action: Identify the starting materials and the end products
solution_steps.explain: Determine if the end product is chemically different from the start.

solution_steps.action: Look for indicators of chemical reaction
solution_steps.explain: Check for heat, light, gas production, or permanent color change.
Chemical changes are usually irreversible, confirming that a new substance has been formed.

concepts.title: Oxidation of Magnesium
concepts.definition: The combustion of magnesium in oxygen to produce magnesium oxide, which further reacts with water to form a basic hydroxide.
concepts.key_idea: Burning magnesium produces a new substance (ash) that forms a base in water.
question_patterns: describe the burning of a magnesium ribbon
what is the nature of the aqueous solution of magnesium ash
write the equation for magnesium reacting with oxygen
is burning magnesium a chemical change
what do you understand by oxidation of magnesium

solution_steps.explain: Magnesium reacts with oxygen to form magnesium oxide (MgO).
MgO reacts with H2O to form Magnesium hydroxide [Mg(OH)2].
Magnesium hydroxide turns red litmus blue, indicating it is a base.

concepts.title: Displacement Reaction of Copper Sulphate
concepts.definition: A reaction where iron displaces copper from a copper sulphate solution, resulting in a color change from blue to green.
concepts.key_idea: Iron replaces copper, forming green iron both sulphate and a brown copper deposit.
question_patterns: why does copper sulphate solution change color when an iron nail is dropped
describe the reaction between iron and blue vitriol
what is the brown deposit on an iron nail in CuSO4 solution
identify the new substances formed when iron reacts with copper sulphate
how does displacement reaction of copper sulphate work

solution_steps.action: Observe initial blue color of copper sulphate
solution_steps.explain: The blue color is due to copper sulphate.
Iron reacts with the solution over time.
Solution turns green (iron sulphate) and brown copper deposits on the nail.

concepts.title: Carbon Dioxide Test
concepts.definition: A chemical test where carbon dioxide gas is indeed passed through lime water, turning it milky because of the formation of calcium carbonate.
concepts.key_idea: The milkiness of lime water is the standard confirmation for CO2 gas.
question_patterns: how do you test for carbon dioxide gas
what happens when CO2 is passed through lime water
why does lime water turn milky
describe the reaction between vinegar and baking soda
state two key points about carbon dioxide test

solution_steps.action: Generate gas using vinegar and baking soda
solution_steps.explain: The reaction produces carbon dioxide.

solution_steps.action: Pass the gas into freshly prepared lime water
solution_steps.explain: CO2 reacts with calcium hydroxide.
Calcium carbonate makes the water appear milky.

concepts.title: Rusting of Iron
concepts.definition: The slow oxidation of iron with both oxygen and moisture to form a flaky brown substance called rust.
concepts.key_idea: Both air (oxygen) and moisture are essential for rusting to occur.
question_patterns: what are the conditions necessary for rusting
write the chemical equation for rusting of iron
why is rusting faster in coastal areas
is rusting a physical or chemical change
explain rusting of iron in your own words

solution_steps.action: Expose iron to air and water
solution_steps.explain: Iron reacts with atmospheric oxygen and water vapor.
The resulting iron oxide is what we call rust.
Without either oxygen or moisture, rusting does not occur, proving both are essential.

concepts.title: Prevention of Rusting
concepts.definition: Methods to protect iron from corrosion by blocking its contact with both oxygen and water, like painting or galvanisation.
concepts.key_idea: Galvanisation involves depositing a layer of zinc on iron to prevent rust.
question_patterns: how can rusting of iron be prevented
what is galvanisation
why are water pipes galvanised
how does painting prevent rusting
how does prevention of rusting work

solution_steps.explain: Use paint or grease to block air and moisture.
Deposit a layer of chromium or zinc (galvanisation) on the iron surface.
A continuous, unbroken coating ensures neither air nor moisture can reach the iron, preventing rust.

concepts.title: Crystallisation
concepts.definition: A physical process used to obtain pure solid crystals of a material from its saturated solution.
concepts.key_idea: Crystallisation is a physical change used for purification.
question_patterns: describe the process of crystallisation
how can you obtain pure copper sulphate crystals
is crystallisation a physical or chemical change
why is dilute sulphuric acid added during copper sulphate crystallisation
explain crystallisation in your own words

solution_steps.explain: Dissolve the substance in hot water until no more dissolves.
Allow the solution to sit undisturbed while cooling.
Pure crystals of the substance will precipitate out.
